housing.intro: Bozeman is the hub: BZN airport, groceries, and the bars are all here, and everything below is inside a two-hour drive. Mid-October is shoulder season — after the summer crush, before Big Sky's ski rates kick in — which is the main reason the numbers work for a group this size.

areas.name: Bozeman / Gallatin Valley
areas.vibe: Walk to Main Street and roll to the airport in 15 minutes. Least scenic, most convenient, easiest place to find a house that genuinely sleeps 10.
areas.quality: Weakest number here (±20%) — no live quotes for 4BR houses. Call Mountain Home Montana or Stay Montana for real figures.

areas.name: Livingston / Paradise Valley
areas.vibe: Emigrant Peak over the Yellowstone River, blue-ribbon fly water out the back door, closest good base for a north-gate Yellowstone day. Also the best value of the six.
areas.quality: Best data on the page — live bookable quotes for your exact dates across six 4-5BR properties, median $393/night.

areas.name: Ennis / Madison Valley
areas.vibe: Fishing-first and genuinely quiet. The Madison is the draw; the town is one street. Note that most homes here post a flat year-round rate, so October saves you little.
areas.quality: Published operator rate tables for four 4BR properties. Only 15-22% below summer — most inventory doesn't discount at all.

areas.name: Big Sky
areas.vibe: Lone Peak scenery and proper ski-town cabins, in the cheapest month of its own year. But summer operations ended Sept 13 and lifts don't spin again until Nov 25 — you'd be there in the dead zone.
areas.quality: Dated operator rate tiers. October ADR ~$673 is Big Sky's annual low — but absolute prices are still the highest of the six.

areas.name: Gardiner
areas.vibe: Yellowstone's north gate, open to cars year-round, with Lamar Valley at sunrise. Tiny town, thin restaurant scene, longest haul from the airport.
areas.quality: Thin — three data points, one from a stale 2018 page. Treat as indicative only.

areas.name: West Yellowstone
areas.vibe: West gate, and the cheapest beds of the six. October is its cheapest month by a wide margin, but ~90% of in-park lodging has already shut, so the town is quiet.
areas.quality: Operator-published ranges from two inns. October averages ~$211/night town-wide.

notes: Your weekend sits in a genuine trough. MSU plays away Oct 17 (home games are Oct 24 and 31), and Montana's general rifle season opens Oct 24 — five days after you leave. One Paradise Valley property runs $527/night on Oct 9-12 and $345 on Oct 23-26; you're in between.

Fees are brutal on a short stay. Cleaning alone runs $240-680 per booking for large Montana properties, which on 3 nights is 15-30% of the nightly subtotal before the platform fee and tax land on top. Budget +40-55% over the headline rate.
Montana charges 8% lodging tax statewide. Big Sky and West Yellowstone add a 4% resort tax on top (12% total). Bozeman, Livingston, Ennis and Gardiner are 8%.
October discounts are not uniform. Paradise Valley runs ~57% under July on the same properties; Ennis barely moves because most homes post flat year-round rates.
Big Sky is the most expensive of the six in absolute terms despite being in its own cheapest month — and it's half-shuttered, with lifts closed from Sept 13 until Nov 25.
Anything sleeping 10 usually means 4-5 bedrooms; Airbnb's guest count includes sofa beds, so read the actual bed list.
Snow is normal by mid-October and nights sit near freezing. Get a plowed driveway and skip anything up a forest road.
housing.sourceNote: Bands come from operator rate calendars, live property-manager quotes and market ADR read Aug 2026. Only Paradise Valley has live quotes for your exact dates — Airbnb, Vrbo and the OTAs all block automated date-locked pricing, so every other figure is indicative. Each area below is labelled with how good its data is.

costs.flightNote: Fares are Kayak trailing-12-month route averages retrieved Aug 2026 — indicative, not quotes for these dates. Oct 16-19 is a Fri-Mon weekend ~2 months out, so expect the upper half of each range.
costs.carNote: BZN is roughly 2.4x Denver for car rental. Minivans are the single most overpriced class here ($148/day vs $109 for a full-size SUV) — take two SUVs instead. One 7-seat SUV will not fit 8 people plus luggage. The majors will not guarantee AWD: you book a class, not a drivetrain, so call the counter. Add ~30% for Montana's 4% vehicle tax, airport concession and license fees.
costs.foodNote: Bozeman has no sales tax on groceries or restaurant meals — menu price is the price. But restaurants run 25-50% above US average while groceries are near par, so cooking is the real saving. Expect 20% auto-gratuity on parties of 8 (Plonk states this explicitly). Costco at 2505 Catron St is 10 min from the airport — natural arrival-day provisioning stop.
